_notes: Fleet config 0.5 (ADR-0040). One concept, the JOB; one axis for evidence, the TIER; one axis for idle work, IDLE.
Hot-reloaded every 60s; history in docs/worklogs. Shipped as a sibling file so the rename and the restart commute.
roster.<name>.tier — how much evidence this model gets. THE only thing that sets a run count.
t0 trial     e90 x1, promotion HELD — it can never climb out on its own.
t1 standard  e90 x3, promotes to t2 on one counted e90 that reached level 5.
t2 long      e90 x3 + e360 x1.
Required on EVERY entry: the roster is a model CATALOG (ADR-0041), so there is no
unscheduled entry left to make an exception for. objective and wikiCoords are REFUSED here —
steering is a campaign, which names the entry under `models` and owns its own task shape.
There is no per-entry override and no per-billing table: a bespoke volume is a NAMED tier in
runner/src/models.ts, reviewed like an episode id, never a number edited into one entry.
A t0 model that earns rung 1 KEEPS the witness (--status shows `t0*`): move it to t1 and it
promotes immediately on evidence it already has, with nothing re-run. Moving a model by hand is
always allowed and never records a promotion — `promoted` is only ever said of a climb.
roster.<name>.idle — what it does with an account once its tier is spent. Absent = none.
none        nothing. What a paid model wants, and the default so idle work is never bought by omission.
unlimited   one freeplay session at a time, unscored, up to 6h on EVERY class (UNLIMITED_SESSION_MS).
The clock is deliberate: a class governs the next pick, never a run in flight, so an endless
session ended only by a 20m idle watchdog holds its account forever.
billing — free or paid, derived (free slug / LAN / claude-code / allowlist -> free; else paid); roster.<name>.billing overrides.
Since 0.5 it says ONLY where a run may physically execute: the account class, and the rate-limit key.
It buys a model no runs and costs it none. Trial a paid model by giving it t0, not by editing a target.
accounts: three classes. An account belongs to exactly one; listing says who may SCHEDULE it, `enabled` says who HOLDS it.
pool  free models, in preference order. Never PROBE, never SMOKE*.
paid  paid picks land only here; with policy.paid present and this empty they are HELD, never spilled.
local a model on the operator's own hardware (isLocalBase) lands only here — the box serves one runner at a time.
A DISABLED pinned job may park on a listed account; an ENABLED one may not (the whole file is refused if it does).
policy: only where runs execute and how many at once. maxConcurrent { <rate-limit key>: n } (concurrencyKeyOf);
paid { maxConcurrent } is the paid throttle. runsPerEpisode and extras are NOT 0.5 keys and are refused by name.
campaigns: probe campaigns, the third lane (ADR-0041). { <name>: { enabled, models "all"|[refs],
runsPerCell, cells [{ id, race?, class?, character?, objective?, ... }], account?, objective?,
wikiCoords?, watchdogs?, maxToolCalls? } }. Every run is an unscored `probing` episode, so a
campaign is never re-armed by a harness bump — that is what separates a probe from an eval.
Precedence: episode-table defaults < campaign < cell. account set = PINNED (same rules as a
pinned job); absent = the policy schedules it, between the evals and the idle work.
Completion is DERIVED (cells x models x runsPerCell vs counted probe runs on disk). A finished
campaign gets enabled:false and KEEPS its results — see the /campaigns page.
queue: jobs { ref | [refs], episode e90|e360|freeplay, repeat n|"loop", enabled, account? }.
account set = PINNED to it (never policy-scheduled); absent = manual pool job, outranks the policy for a pool account.
A waiting manual job reserves the POOL only — the paid and local classes still pick (a226bbb).
preflight: ADR-0023; its accounts may not be in the pool or on a job.

nav-probe.objective: Travel from Coldridge Valley to Ironforge, then take the Deeprun Tram from Ironforge to Stormwind. Use roads and the game's own transport (the tram; flight masters once discovered). Keep a travel log in the scratchpad: destination chosen, route chosen, what worked, what failed and why. In each city, find the flight master and a trainer and note them in the log. Once in Stormwind, keep exploring and questing there.
